I truly believe in educating my patients as much as I can on dental health, to minimize, wherever possible, the chances of an issue arising. Preventive care is key, so let’s work together to keep your family’s teeth and gums healthy! Schedule Now General Dentistry Procedures Here’s a quick overview of some of the common general dentistry procedures that we provide at Prizm Dental & Veneers in Gilbert. Schedule Now   Dental Implants Dental Implants are a permanent solution for missing teeth, providing a strong foundation with a natural look and feel. Implants preserve your jawbone health and restore chewing functionality. Crowns A crown is a custom-made cap placed over a damaged tooth to restore its shape, size, and strength. Crowns are ideal for teeth weakened by decay, fractures, or after root canals. Bridges For patients missing one or more teeth, bridges can fill the gap. They are anchored by crowns on adjacent teeth and provide a seamless, natural appearance while maintaining tooth alignment. Tooth-Colored Fillings Modern fillings are made of composite resin, matching the natural shade of your teeth. This creates an aesthetic, durable solution to cavities without the noticeable look of old-fashioned metal fillings. Clear Braces For those seeking straighter teeth without the visibility of traditional metal braces, clear aligners like Invisalign are an excellent choice. These discreet, removable braces gradually shift teeth into their ideal positions. Root Canals When tooth decay reaches the pulp, a root canal can save the tooth by removing the infected tissue, cleaning the area, and sealing it with a crown for protection. Tooth Extraction In cases where a tooth is beyond saving, extraction becomes necessary to prevent further complications and infection. Dentures For patients missing several teeth, dentures offer a removable, affordable option to restore function and aesthetics, ensuring a complete smile and improved oral health. Sleep Apnea Appliance (Snore Guard) For those who snore, or have trouble breathing at night when muscles relax, a dental appliance could replace a C-PAP machine or prevent you needing one in the future.
